# **Purpose**

For our CTmin and CTmax trials, we set the Arduino system to a desired rate of +/- 0.3°C/minute. However, factors such as temperature dispersal, ambient room temperature, and chilling mechanisms (see Methods in associated paper) may affect the actual rate experienced. Here, we calculated the average temperature rate for each trial type (CTmax, CTmin) and each species (mosquitofish, sailfin, swordtail). We then compare these averages to the goal rate (+/- 0.3°C/min), an alternative minimum rate (-0.1°C/min) and among species to confirm similar rate exposure. 

# **Data**

All rates were calculated in excel (see supplementary data sheets in **Extras** folder) by fitting a simple linear model of temperature by second, then converted to degree/minute. We excluded one trial (Gambusia, CTmin, 7 Nov 23) as the data sheet only captured the second half of the trial. 


All analyses were conducted using R version 4.4.2 


## Load required libraries

Remove the '#' prior to `install.packages` if it is the first time installing library. 

```{r, warning=FALSE}
#install.packages("curl")             #v5.2.1
library(curl)

#install.packages("dplyr")            #v1.1.4
library(dplyr)

#install.packages("tidyr")            #v1.3.1
library(tidyr)

#install.packages("gt")               #v0.11.1
library(gt)

#install.packages("summarytools")     #v1.1.4
library(summarytools)

#install.packages("ggplot2")          #v3.5.1
library(ggplot2)
```


## Read in data

```{r}
# OPTION 1: download 'rate_calc.csv' into working directory 
rates <- read.csv("rate_calc.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
head(rates)


# OPTION 2: load from Github repository
#rates <- curl("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisondavis/Temperature/refs/heads/main/rate_calc.csv")
#rates <- read.csv(rates, header = TRUE, sep = ",", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
#head(rates)

# One trial (Gambusia, CTmin, 7 Nov 23) only captured part of the excel sheet, so the rate calculated does not reflect the whole trial. We will remove this trial.

rates <- rates[-c(24),]

# Rename trial and species levels for more intuitive table labels
rates$Trial <- factor(rates$Trial,
                        levels = c("min", "max"),
                        labels = c("CTmin", "CTmax"))

rates$Species <- factor(rates$Species,
                        levels = c("swordtail", "sailfin", "gambusia"),
                        labels = c("Swordtail", "Sailfin", "Mosquitofish"))


# Will create a separate data set for CTmax and CTmin

max.rates <- rates[rates$Trial =="CTmax",]
min.rates <- rates[rates$Trial =="CTmin",]

```


# **Analysis**

## Summary statistics

**Rates by trial**

Average rates per trial type (CTmax, CTmin) for all species combined.

```{r}

#calculate average rate per trial type
trial.rates <- rates %>%
  group_by(Trial) %>%
  summarize(Rate=mean(Rate, na.rm=TRUE), .groups = "drop")

trial.rates

```

**Rates by species and trial**

Average rates per trail type (CTmax, CTmin) per species (mosquitofish, sailfin, swordtail)

```{r}
#calculate average rate per trial per species
trial.rates2 <- rates %>%
  group_by(Trial, Species) %>%
  summarize(trial.rate=mean(Rate, na.rm=TRUE),
            stand.dev = sd(Rate, na.rm=TRUE),
            min= min(Rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            Median= median(Rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            max= max(Rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

trial.rates2

```


## Normality 

**Results:** Normal, but the sample sizes are so small, so this result is tentative. Will perform a sensitivity analysis to determine if our results rely on individual trials.
```{r}
#check normality
normal <- rates %>%
  group_by(Trial, Species) %>%
summarize(statistic =shapiro.test(Rate)$statistic,
          p.value = shapiro.test(Rate)$p.value)

normal #normal for all trials and all species

```

**Histograms for CTmax and CTmin trials**

```{r}
# 5 bins chosen following Sturges's Rule
hist.max <- ggplot(max.rates, aes(x = Rate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "grey", color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Species) +
  theme_minimal()
hist.max

hist.min <- ggplot(min.rates, aes(x = Rate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "grey", color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Species) +
  theme_minimal()
hist.min


```



## Comparison to target rate

Testing if CTmax trials met a rate of 0.3°C/minute and if CTmin trails met a rate of -0.3°C/minute. Will do this for all trails first, then repeat within species. 

```{r}
# All CTmax and all CTmin trials
t.test(max.rates$Rate, mu=0.3) #significant (p=0.001)
t.test(min.rates$Rate, mu=-0.3) #significant (p<0.001)



# CTmax by species
wt <- max.rates %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarize(statistic =t.test(Rate, mu=0.3)$statistic,
          p.value = t.test(Rate, mu=0.3)$p.value)

wt
### Only swordtail CTmax trial rates differed from 0.3degC/min (p<0.001).




# CTmin by species
wt2 <- min.rates %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarize(statistic =t.test(Rate, mu=-0.3)$statistic,
          p.value = t.test(Rate, mu=-0.3)$p.value) 

wt2
### all species' CTmin trial rates differed from -0.3degC/min (p<0.001 for all).

```

**Alternative CTmin rate**

Due to the difficulties in reaching a -0.3°C/min rate, a common alternative rate for CTmin trials is -0.1°C/min. We will repeat the comparisons above but with a -0.1°C/min rate instead.

```{r}

# All CTmin trials
t.test(min.rates$Rate, mu=-0.1) #not significant (p=0.364)




# CTmin by species
wt3 <- min.rates %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarize(statistic =t.test(Rate, mu=-0.1)$statistic,
          p.value = t.test(Rate, mu=-0.1)$p.value) 

wt3
### No CTmin rates in any species differ from -0.1degC/min.


```



## Differences between species

Since we detected differences from the target rate, we wanted to compare the rates among the species to see if they differed from each other. 

```{r}

oneway.test(Rate~Species, data=max.rates) #not significant (p=0.390)
oneway.test(Rate~Species, data=min.rates) #significant (p=0.012)


# Since CTmin rates did differ between the species, we will perform pairwise comparisons using a Benjamini-Hochberg p adjustment.

pw <- pairwise.t.test(min.rates$Rate, min.rates$Species, pool.sd = FALSE, p.adjust.method = "holm")

pw_df <- pw$p.value %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("group1") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -group1,
    names_to = "group2",
    values_to = "p_adj") %>%
  filter(!is.na(p_adj)) %>% 
  arrange(group1, group2)
pw_df


### Looks like mosquitofish CTmin trials are significantly different than sailfin (p=0.026) and swordtail (p=0.044). 


```


## Sensitivity analysis

**To target rate**

```{r}

loo.target <- rates %>%
  group_by(Trial, Species) %>%
  group_modify( ~ {
    x <- .x$Rate
    goal <- if(.y$Trial == "CTmax") 0.3 else -0.3
    
    loo.p <- sapply(seq_along(x), function (i) { t.test(x[-i], mu = goal)$p.value})
    loo.mean <- sapply(seq_along(x), function(i) { mean(x[-i])})
    
    tibble(
      n = length(x),
      full.p = t.test(x, mu=goal)$p.value,
      min.loo.p = min(loo.p),
      max.loo.p = max(loo.p),
      min.loo.mean = min(loo.mean),
      max.loo.mean = max(loo.mean)) }) %>%
  ungroup()

loo.target

```


**Among species**

```{r}
loo.spp <- rates %>%
  group_by(Trial) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    df <- .x
    
    full.p <- oneway.test(df$Rate~df$Species, var.equal=FALSE)$p.value
    
    loo.p <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function (i) {
      sub.rate <- df$Rate[-i]
      sub.spp <- df$Species[-i]
      
      oneway.test(sub.rate~sub.spp, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value})
    
    tibble(
      Trial = df$Trial[1],
      full.p = full.p,
      min.loo.p = min(loo.p),
      max.loo.p = max(loo.p)) }) %>%
  ungroup()

loo.spp



```



# **Summary**

**Trial rates compared to set rate**

The goal rate for both CTmax and CTmin trials was +/- 0.3°C/min. Both CTmax and CTmin trials were significantly different than the target rate. When separated by species, only swordtails differed in CTmax trials and all species differed in CTmin trials compared to the the target rate. 

When using the alternate CTmin rate of -0.1°C/min, there were no significant differences for any species. 

A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis indicated that the significance of differences between observed and target ramping rates was unchanged by the exclusion of any individual trial. 

***

**Rates among species**

We also compared rates among the species to determine if one species experienced a significantly different rate compared to the others, regardless of target rate. We did not find any differences for CTmax trials but did find a significant difference in CTmin trials. When followed up with a pairwise test (with a Holm p adjustment), we see that mosquitofish trials are significantly different than sailfin and swordtail. 

A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis resulted in similar conclusions for the CTmax trials, but did indicate that the CTmin results are sensitive to the exclusion of individual trials. This is likely because mosquitofish had fewer trials (3 trials) compared to sailfin (6 trials) and swordtails (5 trials).


**Conclusions**
As ramping rates differed from the target rate, and among the species, we will include trial run id (i.e. file.id) in our models. This will account for the differences we see here, as well as the dependence of individuals within the same trial.
